title: Topkapı's New Darphane Museums and the Archaeology Museums: A One-Day Route Plan
excerpt: How to fit the five new museums in Topkapı Palace's restored imperial mint and the renewed Istanbul Archaeology Museums, with their new Gülhane entrance, into one Sultanahmet museum day or two easier mornings.

body.text: Two large museum changes now sit within a few minutes' walk of each other at the top of Istanbul's historic peninsula. In the first courtyard of Topkapı Palace, the restored Darphane-i Âmire, the old imperial mint, has been turned into a group of five new museums. Just downhill, the Istanbul Archaeology Museums have completed a long restoration and moved their main entrance to the Gülhane side. Together they can fill a very rewarding day, or overload it. This guide explains what is where, how to order the visits, and what to check before you set out. It is a route and timing plan, not a ticket comparison.
What opened in the old imperial mint

[Millî Saraylar](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Kurumsal/HaberDetay/1134/TOPKAPI-SARAYI-NIN-YENI-MUZE-ADASI-ULUSAL-BASINDA-GENIS-YER-BULDU), the palace administration, lists five galleries for the Darphane-i Âmire complex: Porcelain, Calligraphy (Hüsn-i Hat), Imperial Arms (Esliha-i Hümâyun), Maps, and Mint and Industrial Tools. It describes more than 10,000 works selected from its collections. Press reports quoting the administration's president give about 10,300 objects; [DHA](https://www.dha.com.tr/gundem/topkapi-sarayinda-10-bini-askin-eserin-bulundugu-5-muze-ziyarete-aciliyor-2966353) breaks this down as roughly 5,300 porcelain pieces, about 2,000 calligraphy works, 2,500 weapons and around 500 industrial objects. DHA reported an opening ceremony on 24 October 2026 with visitors admitted from 25 October; Türkiye Today, writing a few days earlier, expected the opening itself on 25 October, so treat the exact dates as press reports rather than an official announcement. The complex is in the palace's first courtyard and, according to the same reporting, covers about 17,000 square metres across restored buildings.

That scale matters for planning. Five separate collections in a set of historic buildings are not a quick detour on the way to the Harem. Treat the mint as its own visit with its own time budget, rather than something you will 'see on the way out'.
What changed at the Archaeology Museums

According to [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/culture/istanbul-archaeological-museums-renewed-after-extensive-restoration/4061097), the restoration covered the main neoclassical building, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, the Tiled Kiosk, the courtyard and Gülhane Square. The Museum of the Ancient Orient reopened on 6 July with reorganised galleries and lighting, and about 54,000 exterior tiles of the Tiled Kiosk were catalogued and conserved. The main entrance has moved to Gülhane Square, where a visitor reception centre was set up, and objects now line Osman Hamdi Bey Yokuşu, the slope that leads from the square up to the museum.

The ministry's [museum page](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=IAR01&DistId=IAR) gives the address as Alemdar Caddesi, Osman Hamdi Bey Yokuşu, Gülhane. When we checked it on 26 October 2026 it listed opening at 09:00, closing at 18:30 and the ticket office closing at 17:30, showed the museum as open every day and mentioned an audio guide. Those are planning facts for today, not permanent ones: open the page again on the day before you go.
How the two sites fit together

Think of the area as a short, steep triangle. Topkapı's main gate, the Bâb-ı Hümâyun, stands behind Hagia Sophia at the top. The first courtyard with the mint lies just inside. The Archaeology Museums sit below the palace walls, reached from Gülhane Square and the slope. Gülhane Park runs alongside the slope. [Türkiye Today](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/culture/istanbuls-topkapi-palace-to-showcase-over-10000-artifacts-in-5-new-museums-3230704) reported that a second entrance to the mint complex, opposite the Archaeology Museums, was expected to open about a month after the inauguration; until that is confirmed, plan to arrive through the Imperial Gate.
Three ways to plan the day
These are editorial suggestions, not official timings. Adjust them to your pace and to the hours shown on the official pages that week.

items: The full museum day (not Tuesday). Start at Topkapı when it opens and see the palace courtyards and any section you have specifically chosen first, while energy is high. Break for lunch outside the palace. Return to the first courtyard for two or three of the five mint museums, then walk down to the Archaeology Museums for a focused mid-afternoon visit, allowing for the 17:30 ticket-office time listed on the ministry page.

Split over two mornings. Day one: Topkapı palace plus one or two mint museums. Day two: the Archaeology Museums, Gülhane Park and the remaining mint museums. This suits travellers who prefer depth to coverage and is the least tiring version.

The Tuesday plan. Millî Saraylar's [Topkapı page](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/2/topkapi-sarayi) lists the palace as closed on Tuesdays, while the ministry page listed the Archaeology Museums as open daily. Use a Tuesday for the Archaeology Museums and Gülhane Park, and keep Topkapı and the mint for another day.

body.text: With five new museums, the realistic question is which two or three to see properly. Calligraphy and porcelain are strong choices for visitors interested in Ottoman court arts; the arms and map galleries suit history readers; the mint and industrial tools museum explains the building itself. At the Archaeology Museums, decide in advance whether your priority is the main building, the Museum of the Ancient Orient or the Tiled Kiosk, and see that one first. Anything left over is a reason to come back rather than a failure.
What to check before you go

items: Opening days and hours on both official pages: the [Millî Saraylar Topkapı page](https://www.millisaraylar.gov.tr/Lokasyon/2/topkapi-sarayi) and the [ministry museum page](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=IAR01&DistId=IAR). On 26 October the Topkapı page listed the ticket office as open from 09:00 to 17:00; confirm this, and any separate hours for the mint, before you plan your afternoon.

How admission works for the new mint museums. Türkiye Today reported that entry is included in the regular Topkapı Palace ticket, but the official pages we read did not yet spell out how the Darphane-i Âmire museums are ticketed. Check at the Millî Saraylar ticket page or desk whether your ticket covers them, and whether re-entry after lunch is allowed.
Which entrances are open. The Archaeology Museums' main entrance is now on Gülhane Square according to Anadolu Agency; for the mint, check whether the reported second entrance has opened.
Closures for events. The ministry page carried a one-day closure notice for the Archaeology Museums on 24 October 2026; similar notices can appear at short notice.

Your own limits. The route involves slopes and cobbles. If you need a step-free route or seated breaks, use our [museum access planning checklist](/blog/istanbul-museum-access-planning-checklist) to prepare questions for each venue.

body.text: Where this fits in a wider trip

If you are also deciding whether a museum pass makes sense, keep that separate and use our [museum pass or single tickets guide](/blog/istanbul-museum-pass-or-single-tickets) once you know which visits you will really make. Hagia Sophia is next to the palace gate but runs under different arrangements; read the [Hagia Sophia visitor guide](/blog/hagia-sophia-mosque-visitor-guide) before adding it to the same day. For the rest of your stay, our [Istanbul itinerary for three, five or seven days](/blog/istanbul-itinerary-3-5-7-days) and the [Istanbul destination guide](/destinations/istanbul) give the bigger picture. If you would like help building a private museum day, [contact us](/contact).

seo.uniqueValue: A route-and-timing plan for two newly changed sites a few minutes apart, with three day structures (full day, two mornings, Tuesday), a choose-two-or-three rule for the five mint museums and a dated pre-visit check list based on the official pages.

quality.reviewNotes: Primary: Millî Saraylar news item 1134 (five gallery names, >10,000 works); Millî Saraylar Topkapı location page (Tuesday closure, 09:00-17:00 ticket office, Bâb-ı Hümâyun main gate, Darphane in first courtyard); muze.gov.tr IAM page (address, 09:00-18:30, ticket office 17:30, open daily, 24.10.2026 closure, audio guide). Secondary: AA (restoration scope, Gülhane Square entrance, visitor centre, 54,000 tiles, 6 July Ancient Orient reopening); DHA (≈10,300 objects and breakdown, 24 Oct ceremony, visitors from 25 Oct, first courtyard, ~17,000 m2); Türkiye Today (expected second entrance, attributed). Not verified on an official page: ticket coverage of the mint museums, separate mint hours, the second entrance date - readers are told to check. Day plans and time budgets are editorial. Independent review 2026-10-26: opened all six sources and checked every EN claim and the DE/ES/zh-CN/KO versions; removed the unsourced T1 tram stop reference, attributed the reported ticket inclusion to Türkiye Today while keeping it as a check item, noted the 24/25 October date difference between DHA and Türkiye Today, and restored omitted sentences and English-page labels in translations.
